texts.preamble: Hotel Ranchi Ashok Through Its G M ... vs The State Of Jharkhand And Ors on 7 July, 2014 Author: R.R. Prasad Bench: R.R. Prasad In The High Court Of Jharkhand At Ranchi W.P.(C) No. 1057 of 2014 Hotel Ranchi Ashok & Anr. ... ... Petitioners Versus State of Jharkhand & Ors. ... ... Respondents ----- Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice R.R. Prasad ----- For the Petitioners : Mr. Kalyan Roy, Advocate For the Respondent : J.C. to A.G. ----- 04/ 07.07.2014 .
texts.facts: This writ petition is directed against the order dated 10.01.2014 passed by the respondent No.2-Deputy Commissioner-cum-Adjudicating Officer, Ranchi in Food Safety and Standards Case No.03 of 2012-13, whereby and whereunder a sum of Rs.3,00,000/- was imposed upon the accused persons, as penalty, on account of the contravention of the provision of Food Safety and Standard Act, 2006. Out of Rs.3,00,000/-, these two petitioners have been ordered to pay a sum of Rs.50,000/- and the rest of Rs.2,50,000/- is to be paid by the accused No.3-Bihar State Milk Co-operative Federation. It appears that the complainant-Food Safety Inspector, Ranchi collected 800 Grams of 'Paneer' from Hotel Ranchi Ashok for the purpose of its analysis. The said sample was sent before the Analyst and after analysis, it was found that the batch number, which was put in over the packets of Paneer had been not written prominently and hence, it was not readable and, thereby, it was found to be misbranded in terms of provision as contained in Section 3(zf)(C)(i) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. On finding the product to be 'misbranded', a report was submitted before the respondent No.2-Deputy Commissioner-cum-AdjudicatingOfficer, Ranchi, who having found the appellants guilty for contravention of the provision of the said Act, awarded a sum of Rs.3,00,000/- to be paid by the accused persons. Out of it, an amount of Rs.50,000/- was ordered to be paid by these petitioners vide order dated 10.01.2014 passed in Food Safety and Standards Case No.03 of 2012-13. Being aggrieved with that order dated 10.01.2014, this writ petition has been filed. texts.arguments: The said Section reads as follows:- 49. General provisions relating to penalty.- While adjudging the quantum of penalty under this Chapter, the Adjudicating Officer or the Tribunal, as the case may be, shall have due regard to the following:- (a) the amount of gain or unfair advantage, wherever quantifiable, made as a result of the contravention, (b) the amount of loss caused or likely to cause to any person as result of the contravention, (c) the repetitive nature of the contravention, (d) whether the contravention is without his knowledge, and (e) any other relevant factor.
